title: soc2-prep-scratchpad-harper-cole
content:
SOC2 prep - scratchpad (Harper)

Purpose:
- Brain dump of open questions, control mapping ideas, evidence sources, and quick TODOs while prepping for readiness review.
- Highly iterative; expect TODOs and action owners.

Quick status:
- Gap analysis draft done (see Confluence link). Main gaps: periodic access review cadence, proof of encrypted backups for private deployments, and evidence of retention policy enforcement for logs.
- Next milestone: internal readiness review w/ legal + SRE -> target 2024-06-21.

Open risk questions / discussion items:
1) Data classification boundary for Hosted vs Private: do we need separate control evidence for customer-managed KMS in Private? (Maya to confirm with infra)
2) Backup encryption for Dedicated: we use cloud-provider snapshots + encryption at rest — need exportable proof (snapshot config + KMS key ARN). Who owns? (Infra + Platform)
3) Access review frequency: current practice is ad-hoc quarterly for infra team, but no formal ticketed evidence. Proposal: quarterly automated report from Okta + manual sign-off recorded in Confluence. (Owner: Ryan)
4) Incident response drills: we have postmortems but not formal tabletop evidence for SOC2. Schedule 1 tabletop before audit window. (Owner: Harper)

Control mapping notes (rough):
- CC:Access Controls -> Okta groups, SCIM, role-mapping for Redwood Console (evidence: SCIM provisioning logs, group membership export, RBAC policy doc).
- CC:Change Management -> release engineering playbooks, PR reviews, change approvals (evidence: GitHub PR history, release notes, change-approval emails).
- CC:Encryption -> KMS config, CMK rotation policy, customer-managed KMS docs for Private (evidence: KMS policy docs, key rotation logs).
- CC:Logical & Physical Access -> SRE on-call access, bastion/jump-host logs, step-up auth for sensitive operations.
- CC:Monitoring & Logging -> retention policy (how long?), alerting rules, example alerts + evidence of triage. Need to capture retention enforcement e.g., S3 lifecycle policy + ElasticSearch/Datadog retention config.

Evidence inventory (initial):
- Okta: user list export, SCIM sync logs -> path: /confluence/okta-sync (linked)
- GitHub: PRs for infra changes -> JIRA tags + PR links (pull together via search query)
- KMS: key policy docs, rotation logs -> ask infra for exported key activity report
- Backups: snapshot configuration & timeline -> cloud console screenshots + export of snapshot metadata
- Alerts: representative incidents (last 12 months) w/ postmortems -> need to redact customer data before sharing
- Log retention: S3 lifecycle rules + datadog/ES retention cfg -> ask observability team for config exports

Immediate TODOs (by priority):
- [ ] Ryan: produce Okta group membership export + proposed quarterly sign-off template (due 2024-06-14)
- [ ] Maya: confirm backup encryption evidence artifacts for Dedicated + Private (due 2024-06-12)
- [ ] Lena: collect 3 representative postmortems (last 12 months) and redact PII (due 2024-06-16)
- [ ] Harper: schedule tabletop incident drill and draft agenda (target date 2024-06-18)
- [ ] Infra: export KMS key rotation logs for all CMKs used in production (JIRA-SEC-342)

Notes / clippings (raw):
- "Do we treat Private deployment as fully separate system for SOC2 evidence?" -> I think we can map same controls but must show customer-managed keys separately; also network boundaries differ -> separate evidence for firewall rules/VPC configs.
- Slack thread: #security-ops: link to discussion about automatic group sync failures (we should attach to evidence if recurring).
- GitHub PR 621: contains IaC that changed our snapshot lifecycle — check timestamps against claimed retention.

Questions for Legal / Audit desk:
- Are tabletop exercises an absolute requirement or 'recommended'? (Impacts schedule)
- Any preferred form for access review sign-off? E.g., Confluence template vs signed XLS?

Evidence packaging idea:
- Use one Evidence folder per control family with a README.md that lists artifact files, redaction notes, and owner. Keep master index in Confluence (linked).

Risks & mitigation ideas (brainstorm):
- Risk: missing explicit evidence for KMS rotation -> Mitigation: export rotation events and attach.
- Risk: adhoc access reviews -> Mitigation: automated Okta exports + calendar reminders + Confluence sign-off page.
- Risk: customer-managed keys (Private) create inconsistent evidence sets -> Mitigation: document differences in a short appendix per customer deployment type.

Random scratch lines (do not delete):
- check retention policy for logs: datadog prod index -> 90 days? confirm
- do we have a single place that tracks all service owners? (service-owner roster in Confluence seems outdated)
- get a sample of the remediation proof for the last 6 months (tickets closed)

References / links to pull into final evidence pack:
- Confluence: /spaces/SOC2/pages/BASELINE
- Jira: JIRA-SEC-342 (KMS export), JIRA-OPS-112 (backup lifecycle change)
- GitHub PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/621

Next steps:
- Consolidate owner TODOs into JIRA (I will create tickets after confirming owners today).
- Draft the evidence folder structure and share with infra + obs for feedback.

-- Harper
(Notes intentionally informal; capture everything while it's fresh)
